primary_source_check: Primary HTML confirms section C2 Euclidean scope, printed h<=1/beta with no explicit lower bound, source distance factor and h=1/beta rate, and stray gradient before y-x in the intermediate proof pairing.

independent_calculation.negative_step_counterexample: On R take f(t)=t^2/2, alpha=beta=1, h=-1, x=0,y=1. The printed h<=1/beta holds, but T(t)=2t, so the asserted bound requires 2<=sqrt(2), false since 4>2. More generally every h<0 fails this quadratic: (1-h)^2>1-h.
independent_calculation.one_step: For v=y-x, d=grad f(y)-grad f(x), p=<d,v>, the hypotheses give alpha||v||^2<=p, p>=0, ||d||^2<=beta p. From h>=0 and beta h<=1 get h^2||d||^2<=hp, hence ||v-hd||^2<=||v||^2-hp<=(1-alpha h)||v||^2.
independent_calculation.sqrt_boundary: If 1-alpha h<0, the squared estimate rules out v nonzero. For v=0 the bound is 0<=0 with the stated total Real.sqrt. On nontrivial Euclidean source domains alpha<=beta gives the usual nonnegative square-root argument.
independent_calculation.iteration: A supplied global minimizer is a local minimum on the entire space; C1 and Fermat yield zero derivative and actual gradient, thus T(xstar)=xstar. Iteration of the r-Lipschitz inequality yields r^N times the actual initial distance for N>=0.
independent_calculation.exponential: 1-alpha h<=exp(-alpha h) yields sqrt(1-alpha h)<=exp(-alpha h/2), including the total square-root case. Natural powers preserve the bound and exp(-alpha h/2)^N=exp(-alpha h N/2).
independent_calculation.source_specialization: For beta>0, h=1/beta, positive alpha and kappa=beta/alpha>=1, r^N=(1-1/kappa)^(N/2), exp(-alpha h N/2)=exp(-N/(2 kappa)).
